newsitem.title: EGYPT: Israeli Arabs head for Syria in solidarity visit.
newsitem.headline: Israeli Arabs head for Syria in solidarity visit.

text.p: Israeli Arabs will visit Syria on Thursday to express solidarity with its quest for peace and an end to Israeli occupation of the Golan Heights, a delegation member said.

The 44 delegates, including politicians from the opposition Labour and Meretz parties, will visit Syria at the invitation of President Hafez al-Assad, said delegation head Ibrahim Nemer Hussein, who is an independent member of parliament in Israel.

"The delegation visit aims to express the solidarity of the Palestinian public which is inside Israel with Syria in its struggle to achieve peace and its fair demand of ending the Israeli occupation," Abdel-Wahab al-Darawsheh, legislator and leader of the opposition Arab Democratic Party, told reporters at Cairo airport.
Syria wants full withdrawal from the strategic Golan Heights plateau which Israel captured during the 1967 Arab-Israeli war.
"We support Syria's stand on resuming talks (with Israel) from where they stopped on the land-for-peace basis," Darawsheh said.
Israeli-Syrian peace talks ground to a halt in early 1996. There have been no talks since Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ousted Israel's former dovish government in May 1996 elections.
Israel's former Labour government said withdrawal from the Golan would match the depth of peace ties between the two countries.
Labour and Meretz, dovish partners in the last government, favour swapping the heights for peace with Syria -- a policy opposed by right-wing Likud leader Netanyahu.
Last month, Netanyahu joined in giving preliminary approval to a bill that would make it harder for parliament to cede the Golan Heights.
Hussein and Darawsheh slammed Israeli measures against Palestinians in the self-rule areas taken in the wake of a twin suicide bombing at a crowded west Jerusalem market.
Israel suspended a resumption of its talks with the Palestinians and sealed off the West Bank and Gaza after last week's explosions, in which 15 people were killed.
"The latest Israeli measures represent a shameful matter that diminishes the importance of peace. We call on the Israeli government to lift the blockade," Hussein said.

"We are working inside the Israeli arena... to make Israel change its mind regarding the embargo policy," Darawsheh said. "But, Netanyahu seems to be mocking us, the forces of peace and the Arab nation."
Arabs make up about 17 percent of Israel's population.

Airport sources told Reuters the delegates would use temporary Syrian travel documents, due to be issued in Cairo, to go to Syria later on Thursday after a 12-hour stopover. The visit will last eight days.
